chunks: One time, I climbed Mount Abu Qubays while the people were performing the Maghrib prayer. I saw that the sun had not set; rather, it had only gone behind the mountain from the sight of the people. Then I met Abu Abdullah عليه السلام and informed him of that, so he said to me:

"Why did you do that? What you did was bad. You are only to perform it when you no longer see it behind the mountain, whether it has set or gone down, so long as no cloud or darkness covers it. Rather, what concerns you is your eastern horizon and your western horizon, and the people are not required to investigate."

key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the Maghrib salat (prayer), the sunset prayer

ai.seo_question: When does the time of Maghrib salat begin according to this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the practical ruling for the time of Maghrib salat (prayer): people act according to the apparent sunset in their own horizon and are not required to investigate beyond that. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام discourages unnecessary scrutiny and affirms a locally observable standard for determining prayer time.
